checks.invariant: Only the operator (loopback or an SSH tunnel, as the docs describe) can reach the web UI endpoints; a caller is identified or the listening address is restricted.
checks.result: Fails in source. start_server builds ReusableTCPServer(("", port), ...) at visualization.py:1740 (all IPv4 interfaces) and prints 'Serving http://0.0.0.0:{port}' at :1741; there is no --host option in main() (:1749-1778). DatabaseRequestHandler.do_GET (:274-349) performs no authentication, token, Host or Origin check before dispatching to any handler. docs/webui.md:43-46 and :130 describe access through 'ssh -L 8888:localhost:8888', docs/webui.md:140 describes 'ssh -L 8888:compute-node:8888' (which needs a non-loopback listener) and docs/webui.md:189 says 'never expose ports publicly'. Candidate shinka-webui/wildcard-bind-no-auth.

checks.invariant: A web page from another origin that the operator visits cannot read web UI API responses through the operator's browser.
checks.result: Fails in source for every JSON endpoint. send_json_response (:1674-1685) sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' at :1681 unconditionally, and all data endpoints are simple GETs with no credential or custom header, so no preflight is needed. Limits established: handle_serve_plot_file (:1015-1019), handle_download_meta_pdf (:923-929), send_error responses and the SimpleHTTPRequestHandler static fall-through send no CORS header, so those bodies are not readable cross-origin; there is no do_OPTIONS. Candidate shinka-webui/cors-wildcard-json-api. Whether a public-origin page may reach a loopback/private address at all is a browser policy fact (Local/Private Network Access) that source cannot settle.

checks.invariant: No unauthenticated request can change server-side state (write, delete, start a job).
checks.result: Holds. The handler defines only do_GET; no do_POST/do_PUT/do_DELETE/do_OPTIONS exists, so other methods get the stdlib 501. GET handlers only read: ProgramDatabase and SystemPromptDatabase are opened with read_only=True (:464, :558, :628, :727, :1053), which maps to a 'file:...?mode=ro' URI (shinka/database/dbase.py:338). The three plain sqlite3.connect calls (:235, :1145, :1253) are read-write handles but issue only PRAGMA busy_timeout and SELECT statements. The only process-wide mutable state is the in-memory db_cache (:36, :484).

checks.invariant: A request-supplied db_path resolves to a file inside search_root before any file or sqlite access.
checks.result: Fails in source. _get_actual_db_path (:428-430) returns its argument unchanged. The value is passed to os.path.join(self.search_root, ...) at :449, :546, :616, :694, :785, :843, :891, :948, :1035 and :1134 with no normalisation or containment test; an absolute value discards search_root and '../' climbs out of it. Reach established per endpoint: (a) /get_programs, /get_programs_summary, /get_program_count, /get_program_details, /get_database_stats, /get_system_prompts return the contents of any sqlite file with the Shinka 'programs' (or sibling prompts.sqlite 'system_prompts') schema anywhere the server uid can read; a non-sqlite or foreign-schema file yields only an error string. (b) /get_meta_files lists meta_<int>.txt in dirname(db_path) or its meta/ subdirectory and returns absolute server paths (:815). (c) /get_meta_content returns the text of meta_<N>.txt in that directory. (d) 404 versus 500/JSON-error distinguishes existing from missing paths (:452-453, :1136-1138, :796-798). Arbitrary non-sqlite files are NOT readable through db_path alone. Candidate shinka-webui/db-path-traversal.

checks.invariant: The processed_count and generation query values cannot select a file outside the meta or plots directory of the chosen run.
checks.result: Partly holds. /get_meta_content builds meta_{processed_count}.txt (:847) and reads it (:859-860) but int(processed_count) at :863 raises inside the try for any value containing '/', so content is returned only for integer-like values; traversal through this parameter is blocked there. /download_meta_pdf (:895-913) has no int() conversion and returns the file body (as PDF, or as raw text at :918-921 when no converter exists), but the fixed 'meta_' prefix means a '../' sequence only resolves when a directory whose name starts with 'meta_' already exists at that position, and the '.txt' suffix is always appended; no such directory is created by the framework (meta files are written as meta/meta_<int>.txt). /get_plots builds gen_{generation} (:953); because gen_<N> directories do exist in a results directory, generation='0/../../<dir>' lists .png/.gif/.jpg/.jpeg file names in any directory ending in results/plots, names only. Folded into shinka-webui/db-path-traversal as bounded variants.

checks.invariant: /plot_file/ serves only plot images that live inside search_root.
checks.result: Fails in source. handle_serve_plot_file (:981-1025) URL-decodes the remainder of the path (:985), joins it to search_root (:987), tests existence first (:990-992), then compares os.path.abspath strings with startswith and no trailing separator (:995-997). Consequences: (1) no extension or directory allowlist, so every regular file under search_root is returned as application/octet-stream (:1009), while the listing endpoint restricts itself to four image extensions (:961); search_root defaults to the launch directory (:1753, :1781); (2) a sibling whose name extends the root name (root 'results' versus 'results_old', 'results.bak') passes the prefix test; (3) abspath does not resolve symlinks, so a link inside the root is followed out of it; (4) existence is tested before containment, so 404 versus 403 reveals whether any path on the host exists. Paths outside the root that do not share its string prefix are refused with 403. Candidate shinka-webui/plot-file-unrestricted-read.

checks.invariant: Meta text and request values cannot inject commands or active content into the wkhtmltopdf/pandoc conversion.
checks.result: Command injection is refuted: both subprocess.run calls use argument lists without a shell (:1510-1529, :1562-1567) and the only variable arguments are NamedTemporaryFile paths (:1498-1507, :1551-1560). Content injection holds: meta file text is converted with markdown.markdown (:1338-1341), which passes raw HTML through, and is interpolated unescaped into the document at :1492 and written to the file handed to the renderer (:1501, :1554). The request value 'generation' is also interpolated unescaped at :1369 and :1489-1490, but it is only reachable when a file literally named meta_<that value>.txt exists (:902-904), so it is not attacker-reachable from the network alone. Candidate shinka-webui/meta-pdf-html-injection for the meta text path.

checks.invariant: The static fall-through to SimpleHTTPRequestHandler serves only the packaged web UI assets.
checks.result: Holds. start_server calls os.chdir(webui_dir) (:1723-1729) before the server is built, the handler is constructed without a directory argument (:40-42, :1714-1715), so the stdlib handler serves the package's webui directory (HTML shells, two images, and the visualization.py source). Path normalisation is the stdlib translate_path. Nothing operator-specific is stored there. Unmatched API routes (for example a data route without db_path) also land here and return the stdlib 404.

checks.invariant: File paths stored inside a database or failure.json cannot direct the server to read files outside search_root.
checks.result: Fails in source, but only for an author of on-disk state. _read_failure_json joins details.failure_json_path from the attempt_log table to search_root (:75) and _resolve_failed_node_code_path joins artifacts.generated_code_path from that JSON (:134); an absolute value replaces the root. The file text is returned as 'code' by /get_program_details for id 'failed:proposal:<gen>' (:196, :700-711). In normal runs both values are written by the framework, not by model output (shinka/core/async_runner.py:3173, :3298). Recorded as a variant inside shinka-webui/db-path-traversal; it needs a crafted database plus JSON file on the server's disk.

checks.invariant: A request value placed in a response header cannot split the response.
checks.result: Not reachable. processed_count is placed in Content-Disposition at :925-927, but that line is reached only after os.path.exists succeeds for a file literally named meta_<processed_count>.txt (:899-904); a value containing CR/LF therefore needs a pre-existing file with those bytes in its name.

checks.invariant: Model-derived database fields are HTML-escaped (or set through textContent) before they reach innerHTML or d3 .html() in viz_tree.html.
checks.result: Fails in source for several fields while neighbouring fields are escaped. Unescaped: metadata.patch_name in the node summary (:5688, :5692-5693), the patch panel (:5849, :5953), tree tooltips (:4758, :4770-4786, and the island-tree copy at :10406-10413), heatmap and MAP tooltips (:8860, :11017) and the best-path timeline (:10681); metadata.patch_description (:5850, :5857-5858, :10679); metadata.thought through marked.parse (:6009, sink :6022); meta file text through marked.parse (:3073, :3076) and through formatProgramSummaries/processSimpleMarkdown with no escaping (:2913-2914, :2956-2961), sink :3042; system-prompt name and description (:17656, :17660, sink :17642); metric keys (:5713, :5722); data.id, data.parent_id and data.error (:5694-5697). Escaped correctly: code (:5634), text_feedback (:5832), metadata values (:5737, :5748, :5756), stdout/stderr logs (:6101, :6105), llm_result (:6161-6170), diffs (:6322), failure summary (:6531-6534), plot file names (:6283-6284). The page has no CSP and no sanitizer; marked is loaded unpinned from a CDN (:2077) and current marked releases pass raw HTML through. Candidate shinka-webui/dom-xss-llm-derived-fields.

checks.invariant: Browser-controlled document state (location, storage, messages) does not reach an HTML sink directly.
checks.result: Holds for direct flows. The only location reads are db_path, left_tab, right_tab and selected_node (:3421-3433, :4056, :9125-9167). db_path is sent to the server with encodeURIComponent and shown through escapeHtml (:5187, :5301); left_tab is used only inside a querySelector string (:9152); selected_node is used only as a lookup key (:8273-8292). There is no postMessage listener, document.write, eval or string timer. Relevance to the candidate: db_path from the URL is loaded even when it is not in the server's database list (:3433) and selected_node auto-selects a node (:9167), so a single link can load a chosen database and render one node's details without a click.

checks.invariant: index.html and compare.html do not render model-derived text as HTML.
checks.result: Holds for model-derived text: both pages render only database paths and labels, all through escapeHtml (index.html:689, :745-751; compare.html:448), and numeric statistics. Residual, not model-reachable: index.html writes formatter output with innerHTML (:854) and formatBestGeneration/formatGenerations (:929-937, :956-958) would pass a non-numeric MAX(generation) value through unescaped; that needs a hand-crafted sqlite file whose generation column holds text, so it is recorded as hardening only.

candidates.title: /plot_file/ returns any file under the search root (by default the launch directory that holds .env) and its prefix check admits sibling directories and symlinks
candidates.description: Lower-trust principal: any client that can send an HTTP GET to the web UI port (the server listens on all interfaces without authentication; see shinka-webui/wildcard-bind-no-auth). Accepted input: the URL path after /plot_file/. Control that should stop it: the 'Security check: ensure the path is within search_root' in handle_serve_plot_file. Crossed boundary: network client to operator files. The handler is meant to serve plot images that /get_plots lists (png/gif/jpg/jpeg only), but it applies no extension or sub-directory restriction, so every regular file under search_root is returned as application/octet-stream. search_root defaults to the current working directory, and the documented quick start runs 'shinka_visualize --port 8888' with no directory from the project/launch directory, which is also where the docs tell the operator to keep a .env file with provider API keys and where shinka loads it from. GET /plot_file/.env would then return those keys. Three further weaknesses in the same check: (1) containment is a string startswith on abspath values with no trailing separator, so a root of .../results also admits .../results_old/ or .../results.bak via '../results_old/...'; (2) abspath does not resolve symlinks, so a link placed inside the root is followed out of it; (3) existence is tested before containment, so 404 versus 403 tells the client whether an arbitrary host path exists. Limits: paths outside the root that do not share its string prefix are refused; the response carries no CORS header, so a cross-origin page cannot read it directly (a same-origin script, see shinka-webui/dom-xss-llm-derived-fields, can).
candidates.claimed_root_cause: handle_serve_plot_file treats 'inside search_root by string prefix' as the whole authorisation decision: it has no file-type or plots-directory allowlist, compares un-normalised prefixes without a path separator, uses abspath instead of realpath, and checks existence before containment.

trace.description: Any GET whose path starts with /plot_file/ is dispatched to handle_serve_plot_file with no caller check.
The remainder of the URL path is percent-decoded into rel_path, so encoded '../' sequences survive any client-side normalisation.
rel_path is joined to search_root; no extension, directory or file-type restriction is applied.
Containment is abspath(abs_path).startswith(abspath(search_root)) with no trailing separator and no symlink resolution.
The file is opened in binary mode and its full content is written to the response.

evidence.description: root_directory defaults to os.getcwd(), so search_root is the launch directory unless the operator passes a results directory.
Documented remote launch is 'shinka_visualize --port 8888' with no directory argument.
Docs instruct the operator to create a .env file with provider API keys in the project root.
shinka loads .env from the launch (current working) directory, the same directory the web UI serves by default.
The listing endpoint restricts plots to .png/.gif/.jpg/.jpeg, showing the intended scope that the serving endpoint does not enforce.
Unknown extensions fall back to application/octet-stream instead of being rejected.
os.path.exists runs before the containment check, giving a 404-versus-403 existence oracle for any host path.

Build the handler as tests/test_visualization_meta.py does (DatabaseRequestHandler.__new__, search_root=str(T/'root'), stub send_response/send_header/end_headers, record send_error calls, wfile=io.BytesIO(); stub the 'markdown' module if it is not installed). candidates.title: db_path query value is joined to search_root without containment, exposing Shinka databases, prompt databases and meta_*.txt files anywhere on the host
candidates.description: Lower-trust principal: any client that can send a GET to the web UI (network client, or a cross-origin page because these responses carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). Accepted input: the db_path query value on ten endpoints, plus generation/processed_count. Control that should stop it: _get_actual_db_path, which the handlers call first and which is a no-op. Crossed boundary: the operator chose one directory (search_root) to expose; the client reads outside it. What is actually reachable, established from source: (1) /get_programs, /get_programs_summary, /get_program_details, /get_program_count and /get_database_stats return the contents (program source, metrics, metadata including stored LLM prompts/responses and logs) of any sqlite file with the Shinka 'programs' schema that the server uid can read, addressed by absolute path or '../'; (2) /get_system_prompts returns prompts.sqlite from the same out-of-root directory; (3) /get_meta_files lists meta_<int>.txt in an arbitrary directory and returns absolute server paths; /get_meta_content returns the text of such a file; (4) /download_meta_pdf returns meta_<value>.txt and, only where a directory named meta_* already exists, any reachable .txt file; (5) /get_plots lists image file names in any directory ending in results/plots; (6) status differences reveal whether arbitrary files and directories exist and whether a file is a sqlite database. Not reachable through db_path alone: arbitrary non-sqlite files (they produce only an sqlite error string). Variant with a different precondition: path values stored inside a database (attempt_log details.failure_json_path) and inside the referenced failure.json (artifacts.generated_code_path) are also joined to search_root without containment and the referenced file is returned as 'code', so a crafted database placed on the server's disk turns /get_program_details into an arbitrary text-file read; in normal runs those values are written by the framework.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: No function confines request- or database-supplied relative paths to search_root: _get_actual_db_path returns its input unchanged and every handler passes the result straight to os.path.join(self.search_root, ...), where an absolute value replaces the root and '..' segments are never normalised or checked.

trace.description: db_path is taken verbatim from the query string of an unauthenticated GET /get_programs.
The value passes through _get_actual_db_path, which returns it unchanged (definition at line 428-430).
os.path.join(self.search_root, actual_db_path): an absolute value discards search_root, '../' climbs out of it; only os.path.exists is checked afterwards.
The out-of-root file is opened as a read-only ProgramDatabase and all programs are loaded.
The full program list (code, metrics, metadata) is serialised to the client with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

evidence.description: _get_actual_db_path body is 'return db_path'; its docstring calls it a no-op.
Sibling join site in handle_get_programs_summary; the same pattern repeats at lines 616, 694, 785, 843, 891, 948, 1035 and 1134.
handle_get_meta_content opens meta_<processed_count>.txt under the attacker-chosen directory and returns its text.
int(processed_count) limits this endpoint to integer-like file suffixes; it is the only value check on any of these parameters.
handle_get_meta_files returns the absolute filesystem path of each meta file to the client.
handle_get_plots interpolates the raw generation value into a path component, allowing '../' after an existing gen_<N> directory.
handle_get_database_stats opens the attacker-chosen path with a plain read-write sqlite3.connect and returns the sqlite error text for non-database files.
Variant: generated_code_path from failure.json is joined to search_root without containment and the file is later read and returned as 'code' (read at line 196).

candidates.title: Web UI listens on all interfaces with no authentication while the documentation describes access through an SSH tunnel to localhost
candidates.description: Lower-trust principal: any host that can open a TCP connection to the operator's machine on the chosen port (other users of a shared GPU server or cluster network, other devices on the same LAN). Accepted action: any GET request. Control that should stop it: none in source; the listening address is the empty string (all IPv4 interfaces) and there is no option to change it, no token, and no Host or Origin validation. The documentation's remote workflow starts the server on the remote machine and reaches it through 'ssh -L 8888:localhost:8888', which only requires a loopback listener and leads an operator to assume the service is tunnel-only; the same page separately shows a cluster tunnel to a compute node's own address and a one-line 'never expose ports publicly' note. Crossed boundary: network client to operator data. Affected resources: every evolved program, metric, stored LLM prompt/response and log in the served databases, system prompts, meta summaries, and through the two file-handling candidates (shinka-webui/plot-file-unrestricted-read, shinka-webui/db-path-traversal) any file under the launch directory such as .env and Shinka databases elsewhere on the host. The absence of Host validation also leaves the loopback case open to DNS rebinding from a web page. This candidate is limited to exposure of the read-only API; no state-changing endpoint exists.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: start_server hard-codes the bind address to "" and the request handler has no notion of a caller, so reachability of the port is the only access control and it is wider than the documented localhost/SSH-tunnel model.

trace.description: ReusableTCPServer(("", port), handler_factory) listens on every IPv4 interface; main() offers no host option.
Requests are routed purely on path and query; there is no authentication, token, Host or Origin check on any branch.
Database contents are written to whichever peer connected.

evidence.description: The startup banner itself prints 'Serving http://0.0.0.0:{port}'.
The only operator hint is 'remember to forward the port if this is a remote host', which implies a tunnel rather than direct exposure.
Documented remote access is an SSH local forward to localhost:8888 on the remote host.
Cluster example forwards to compute-node:8888, which works only because the server is not loopback-bound; every other cluster user can reach the same address.
Strongest visible control is advisory text: 'Use SSH tunnels for remote access; never expose ports publicly'.
Example of what an unauthenticated peer can obtain: /plot_file/ opens and returns files under the launch directory.

candidates.title: Every JSON endpoint answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, letting any web page the operator visits read run data through the operator's browser
candidates.description: Lower-trust principal: a web page from an unrelated origin opened in the browser the operator uses for the web UI (including when the operator correctly uses an SSH tunnel and a firewalled host). Accepted action: a simple cross-origin GET (fetch or XHR without credentials or custom headers) to http://localhost:<port>/... Control that should stop it: the browser same-origin policy, which the server switches off by sending Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every JSON response; there is no Origin check and no secret in the URL. Crossed boundary: foreign web origin to operator data. Readable cross-origin: /list_databases, /get_programs, /get_programs_summary, /get_program_details (program source), /get_system_prompts, /get_meta_files, /get_meta_content, /get_plots, /get_database_stats, and, combined with shinka-webui/db-path-traversal, Shinka databases and meta files outside the served directory. Not readable cross-origin: /plot_file/ bodies, the PDF download, error bodies and static files (no CORS header). The page needs the port number; 8000 is the default and 8888 is the documented value.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: send_json_response unconditionally emits Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for an unauthenticated API whose only intended client is the same-origin web UI, so the wildcard serves no functional purpose and removes the one browser-side barrier.

trace.description: A cross-origin simple GET issued by a foreign page in the operator's browser is routed like any other request; the Origin header is never read.
Program summaries (including full metadata) are passed to send_json_response; the other data handlers do the same.
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is attached to the response, so the browser hands the body to the foreign page's script.

evidence.description: send_json_response is the single helper used by all JSON endpoints, so the wildcard applies to every one of them.
Limit: the /plot_file/ response sets only Content-Type, Content-Length and Cache-Control, so it is not readable cross-origin.
DEFAULT_PORT is 8000, a predictable target for a foreign page.
The shipped front end calls the API with same-origin relative URLs, so it does not need any CORS header.

candidates.title: Meta summary text is converted to HTML without sanitisation and rendered by wkhtmltopdf on the server when a PDF is requested
candidates.description: Lower-trust principal: the author of meta_<N>.txt, which in a normal run is the meta-summariser model's output and in a shared-results scenario is whoever produced the results directory the operator is viewing. Accepted input: the file text. Control that should stop it: none; Python-Markdown passes raw HTML through and the result is interpolated into a full HTML document. Sink: that document is written to a temp file and opened by wkhtmltopdf (JavaScript enabled by default, file:// origin) or, failing that, pandoc. Crossed boundary: file content to a headless browser running with the web UI process's filesystem and network position. Any GET /download_meta_pdf triggers it, including from an unauthenticated network client, and the rendered PDF is returned to the requester. If the installed wkhtmltopdf permits local file access or network requests from a local document, injected markup such as an iframe/img/script could place local file content into the PDF or make requests to internal addresses. Bounds established from source: the subprocess calls use argument lists with temp-file paths only, so there is no command injection; the request-supplied 'generation' value is also interpolated unescaped into the document but is reachable only when a file literally named meta_<value>.txt exists; wkhtmltopdf and pandoc are optional external tools that are not installed by the package, and when both are missing the raw text is returned instead. Note that on the host where the evolution itself runs, generated programs already execute as the same user, so the added reach matters mainly when results are viewed on a different machine or come from a third party.
